verdict.text:
Track 1 is not measurable on this run. Every slot has `support_gold_missing = 0` and every `gold_slots` entry is an empty string, so the zeros in precision, recall and F1 are artifacts of unpopulated gold labels, not model failures. The adjudication step has evidently not been run for these 30 requirements. This is worth stressing because the raw human conversions in `worst_examples` plainly do contain missing-slot judgements — for 496-Signal two of three annotators emitted `<MISSING_...>` for nearly every slot — so the labels exist in the source material and simply have not been consolidated into the gold record. Until that is done, nothing can be said about fabrication rates, and the single case where the LLM did flag anything (1504-Signal, scope and condition) cannot be credited or penalised.

That said, the qualitative pattern in the examples is exactly the failure mode the study is built to detect, and it is visible even without scoring. On the thinnest inputs the model manufactures a requirement out of the title. 83-Signal has no description at all, yet the output asserts "the system must synchronize identity keys"; two of three humans marked the whole thing missing. 4333-Signal is a bare URL and becomes a confident functional statement. 1504-Signal is essentially noise ("how about we edit this one too? or just delete it") and still yields "the system must edit the notification color". 828-Signal shows a subtler variant: the model invents an actor, "the group administrator", that appears nowhere in the source, where all three humans kept the actor as the app or the user. These are the cases with the lowest similarity (0.18, 0.22, 0.35), which is consistent — the model diverges precisely where the source is underspecified.

The similarity comparison should be read cautiously. llm_vs_human (0.637 seq / 0.515 Jaccard) sits marginally above human_human (0.576 / 0.473), but with standard deviations near 0.27–0.31 and ~89 non-independent pairs from 30 items, that gap is noise. More importantly, the human–human ceiling is depressed by exactly the disagreement described above: when one annotator writes all-MISSING placeholders and another writes prose, their similarity is 0, so the ceiling partly measures policy disagreement about flagging rather than wording. "At the human ceiling" here does not mean "as good as a human".

Paska is clean at 83%, and the five failures are low-severity: three imprecise verbs, all in the system-response segment (592, 6031, 7310), one passive condition, and one non-atomic output at 6457 — notable only because the input set was pre-filtered to atomic requirements, so the model introduced that split itself.

The blocking next step is adjudication: populate `gold_slots` and re-score. As an interim, a majority vote over the `<MISSING_*>` markers already present in the human conversions would give a usable proxy today.
